title: The worked example
blurb: Two SCCs. The cycle 0 → 1 → 0 has mean 2, but leaving to state 2 earns 3, so the bound lets cascade skip Karp on it.

title: An exact fraction
blurb: A 3-cycle of total 7 has gain 7/3. Every gain on this site is an exact fraction, never a rounded float.

title: The policy trap
blurb: Both states have gain 1, yet the 2-cycle earns 0. Keeping the gain is not enough to pick a good action.

title: When δₖ stalls
blurb: A 2-cycle with weights 0 and 10: λ = 5, but δₖ = 10 for every k, so the δ bound never gets close.

title: Gains rise to the sink
blurb: Five SCCs in a chain, each worse than the next. Every SCC but the sink can be skipped.

title: Gains fall to the sink
blurb: The same chain reversed. Each SCC beats everything after it, so no sound bound can skip anything.

title: A long best cycle
blurb: One SCC whose best cycle has length 3. The δ bound needs many rows before it says anything useful.

title: Hard for Howard
blurb: Asadi, Chatterjee and de Raaij (2025) built this family so policy iteration needs many rounds.

title: A random graph
blurb: 14 states, at most 2 actions each. Most SCCs are single states; a few hold the interesting cycles.

title: A benchmark graph
blurb: The example graph from Dasdan's 2004 benchmark suite: 18 states and 6 SCCs.
